Ravi Patel: Heads up — last night around 02:12 UTC we got a burst of ECC/Xid alerts in us-west-2 that only lasted 30–90s but triggered two automatic drains. DCGM exporter shows short blips on cards 0/1/2 on nodes gpu-pool-17. No pod-level OOMs.
Anna Kim: Ugh. Those short blips have been noisy lately. Did the alerts use the current `consecutive_count` rule or the older instantaneous threshold? :thinking:
Ravi Patel: Instantaneous. The rule is firing on `dcgm_ecc_errors_total > 0` with `for: 30s`. I think we should try a sample-decay approach so a single spike doesn't immediately escalate to drains.
Mike Torres: Agree we should avoid unnecessary drains. Proposal: switch to a moving median (1m) + a decaying-count over 5m so old spikes fade out instead of accumulating forever. That keeps sensitivity for sustained errors but ignores 1–2 ephemeral blips.
Anna Kim: Can you sketch the promql? I want to see how it behaves in a replay.
Mike Torres: Sure — rough POC rule:
```
# decaying_count: each scrape adds 1, but the counter decays by 0.5 every minute
decay_count = sum_over_time((dcgm_ecc_errors_total > 0)[5m:30s]) - (rate(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m]) * 0)
# simplified practical expression: require median>0 over 1m and a 5m weighted sum > 1.5
expr: (quantile_over_time(0.5, dcgm_ecc_errors_total[1m])) > 0 and (increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m]) + increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[5m]) * 0.5) > 1.5
```
Ravi Patel: That looks reasonable as a start. We should also add a label for `consecutive_windows` so the alert only marks `severity:critical` after 2 windows in a row (to avoid draining on the very first multi-card burst).
Cassandra (oncall): Important: playbook change too — don't auto-drain until `streak >= 2` or `total_ecc_in_10m >= 5`. We've had false positives where a transient driver hiccup caused a cascade. Update runbook link: https://go/redwood/runbooks/gpu-health
Alex Chen: Cost note — every unnecessary drain causes pods to reschedule and GC snapshots which bumped egress in the last incident. Reducing churn reduces cost and risk. :+1:
Anna Kim: How do we validate this? I can run a historical replay against Prometheus TSDB and produce an alert timeline. If it suppresses the noisy nights but still catches the real degradations, we can roll it to canary.
Mike Torres: I'll put together a small fault injector we can run in a canary pool — it will emit brief ECC-like spikes (simulated gauge) so we can test the decay/sensitivity without risking hardware.
Ravi Patel: Plan: 1) Anna runs replay using last 30 days (esp the 02:00–04:00 window). 2) If pass, deploy new rule to `prometheus-canary` with `severity:warning` for 24h. 3) Run the injector on 1 canary node during low traffic. 4) If stable, promote to prod with `streak>=2` gating. Target: this Friday 03:00 UTC for canary.
Anna Kim: I'll run the replay today and post graphs here. Can someone grant me read access to the long-retention TSDB index? I need the 90d chunk.
Alex Chen: Granted — you should have `prom_read_long` now.
oncall-bot: Automated summary: 4 ECC alerts and 2 Xid alerts fired across 3 nodes between 2026-02-11T02:10:47Z and 2026-02-11T02:11:59Z. No pod evictions recorded.
Cassandra (oncall): One more safety ask: keep `manual: true` on drain runbook by default. Auto-drain only for nodes with `hw_error_streak >=3` and `io_errors > 10` in 10m.
Ravi Patel: Agreed. I'll draft the prom rule PR and a short README explaining the decay rationale and the fallback criteria. Will ping infra-approvers once the replay graphs are attached.
Mike Torres: I'll prep the injector and a kubejob for the canary. Will include the exact promql used for the canary rule so it's reproducible.
Anna Kim: Uploaded replay graphs: https://go/redwood/graphs/replay/3001234567 (look for the median vs instantaneous comparison). Initial impression — decay version reduced noise by ~78% on those nights while still flagging the two longer failures.
Ravi Patel: Nice. I'll open PR against `infra/monitoring` with the rule, changelog entry, and playbook edits. Tagging @eng-sre for review.
Anna Kim: :rocket:
